name: Battery power conversion system
summary: The bidirectional inverter stage of a battery plant that charges and discharges the DC battery from the AC network.
description: The power conversion system is the bidirectional converter that sits between the battery DC bus and the AC network in a storage plant. It charges the battery by rectifying AC and discharges it by inverting DC, under the direction of a plant controller that sets active and reactive power or operates in a grid-forming mode.

Drawings show a converter box with both AC and DC marks and a bidirectional energy-flow arrow, a DC breaker or switch on the battery side, and an AC breaker, filter and often a medium-voltage skid transformer on the network side. Several PCS units may share one transformer.

The symbol does not tell you whether the unit can black-start a dead bus, how much overload it can supply or how it limits fault current. Those features drive protection settings and must be read from the converter specification.
readingNotes: Look for the bidirectional energy-flow qualifier to confirm charge and discharge capability.
Check the transformer and filter on the AC side.
drawingChecklist: State kW, kVA and DC voltage window.
Show DC and AC switching and filters.
Reference control modes and black-start capability.
distinction: A PCS is a utility or commercial storage converter; an inverter-charger is a smaller low-voltage unit with an integral AC transfer relay.
